clue.text: Intends to circle island in poor health, getting uninterrupted progress

indicators.note: to circle means the word for intends goes round the letter for island

parts.note: to intend something is to plan it
someone in poor health is ailing

explanation.surface: Someone means to go round an island while unwell, yet keeps moving forward without trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to circle' puts I inside PLANS to make PLAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a smooth course with no setbacks, from a ship moving easily without tacking.

clue.text: Scroll worthless reading matter on your meeting with American

parts.note: pap is trivial, insubstantial writing
YR is the written abbreviation of your

explanation.surface: Someone browses a scroll of trashy text you share with an American.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient scrolls were made from sheets of this reed-based writing material.

clue.text: Overall interest payable before working

indicators.note: before means the interest letters come first in this down answer

parts.note: APR, annual percentage rate, is interest payable on a loan
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Total interest due before the job begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overall' looks like an adjective meaning total; it is a noun, a protective garment.
explanation.definitionFit: An overall is a protective garment worn over clothes, and so is an apron.

clue.text: Doctor sees end in poverty!

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A physician recognises that being poor is ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician but is the anagram signal on SEES END IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in want, lacking money and necessities, is a state of being poor.

clue.text: Pseudonym one's forgotten, unfortunately

indicators.note: forgotten means the letter for one is lost from the other word

parts.note: an alias is an assumed name
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone sadly can no longer remember their pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection of regret, used to say that sadly something is so.

clue.text: Writing that's seen on face on clock?

definitions.meaning: handwriting done in full rather than in shorthand or type
a clock face shows a minute pointer, the longer of its two

explanation.definitionFit: The script sense is ordinary penmanship; the clock sense is the minute pointer.

clue.text: River running through where ginseng's raised ;

indicators.note: raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
's here means has: the words before it hold the hidden answer

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A river flows past where ginseng is cultivated.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' reads upward; the hidden word REGIN, spanning 'where ginseng's', reversed. The indicator for the hiding is implicit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Niger is a great West African river, which flows through several countries.

clue.text: Panorama may be in favour of religious group seizing power

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: seizing means the religious group grabs the power letter and holds it inside

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A view may be backed by a church faction grabbing control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizing' puts P inside SECT to make SPECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a broad view of a landscape, which a panorama is.

clue.text: Analyses a second and speaks

parts.note: speaks and says are synonyms

explanation.surface: Someone examines something for a moment and then talks.
explanation.definitionFit: To assay is to test a metal or substance to find its makeup, a type of analysis.

clue.text: Simple boxes or empty case for ceramic ware

indicators.note: boxes means the plain word encloses the other letters, as a box holds things

parts.note: simple and plain are synonyms

indicators.note: an empty case keeps only its outside letters, the middle removed

explanation.surface: Plain packaging or an empty crate used for shipping china.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves only the outer letters of 'case'; 'boxes' has the plain word wrap round them, splitting after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain is a fine type of ceramic, such as china cups and plates.

clue.text: Pulls a face, seeing weapons across river

indicators.note: across means the weapons word stretches over the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: guns are weapons

explanation.surface: Someone grimaces on seeing armed men on the far side of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To gurn is a British word for making a grotesque facial expression, as in gurning contests.

clue.text: With detectives chasing, managed to get off!

indicators.note: chasing means the detectives come behind, following the other piece

parts.note: managed, as in ran a business
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's police detectives

explanation.surface: With police detectives in pursuit, a suspect succeeds in getting away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of 'get off' (escape), but alone it is the definition, as in milk that has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Off describes food gone bad, and rancid means spoiled and foul-smelling, especially of fats.

clue.text: Daily newspaper's millions — a force of attraction!

parts.note: a daily or char is a British term for a cleaning woman who comes in by the day
the i is a British newspaper, and its possessive 's adds S
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A daily paper's millions of readers show its huge pull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper description but is a cleaner, a CHAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is personal magnetism, a compelling attractiveness that draws others in.

clue.text: Son does nothing, but edges along warily

parts.note: someone who does nothing idles

explanation.surface: A lazy son, inactive, creeps about cautiously.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidle is to move furtively or sideways, edging in a cautious, sneaking way.

clue.text: Germany have players low in spirits

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
to have something is to own it
a cast is the players in a production

explanation.surface: Germany has a team that is feeling glum.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast is dejected, the state of having low spirits and feeling sad.

clue.text: Ship carrying cargo of loose ginger produces snorts

indicators.note: carrying cargo of means the ship holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: SS, steamship, stands for a ship

indicators.note: loose means the letters of ginger are set free into a new order

explanation.surface: A vessel whose hold of spilled ginger makes people splutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snorts' reads as a verb but is a plural noun here, the same as the answer; 'loose' rearranges the ginger, which 'carrying cargo of' puts inside the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Snorts here are suppressed, sneering laughs, which is what sniggers are.

clue.text: Develop a drug with revolutionary fix for cell

indicators.note: develop signals the letters of a drug are worked into a new shape
revolutionary means turned around, so the fix word is read in reverse

parts.note: to moor a boat is to fix it in place

explanation.surface: Create a narcotic with a radical remedy for a cell, perhaps a biological one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Develop' turns A DRUG into GUARD; 'revolutionary' turns MOOR into ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardroom is where soldiers under arrest are held, a military cell.

clue.text: Impetus gained from minute show of hesitation

parts.note: a minute is a moment, a short time
um is the sound someone makes when hesitating

explanation.surface: Drive comes from a brief pause for thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum is driving force or forward impulse, just as impetus is.

clue.text: Men jump for chance of redemption here

parts.note: pawns are the chess men in the front row
to hop is to jump

explanation.surface: Chess pieces leap at a chance of being saved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redemption' sounds religious, but it is reclaiming a pledged item for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledged item can be redeemed at a pawnbroker's by repaying the loan, so it is a place of redemption.

clue.text: The last character cutting copra concocted something for depression

indicators.note: cutting means the final letter slices into the rearranged letters
concocted means the letters of copra are mixed into a new order

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A final mark slicing through dried coconut, made into a remedy for low mood.
explanation.walkthrough: COPRA is dried coconut meat; 'concocted' turns it into PROCA, with Z cut in.
explanation.definitionFit: Prozac is a brand-name antidepressant drug, a treatment for depression.

clue.text: Fine performer's important part

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
an actor is a performer; the 's stands for 'is', linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A good performer is essential to the show.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is a contributing element, a component that matters to an outcome.

clue.text: Old boy's on unlimited notice to support Queen — it's automatic

indicators.note: to support means in this down answer the other pieces sit under the Queen's letter

parts.note: R, for Regina, means queen
OB stands for old boy, a former pupil; the 's is 'is'

indicators.note: unlimited means the ends of notice are removed

explanation.surface: A former pupil holds back news while backing the monarch, mechanically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' strips N and E from NOTICE to leave OTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotic means acting mechanically, without thought, like an automaton.

clue.text: Previously finished quick examination

parts.note: once means at an earlier time, formerly
something finished is over

explanation.surface: Something done before and completed is a brief inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: A once-over is a rapid, cursory look or inspection of something.

clue.text: Power specs and speed

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of spectacles
mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: Specifications for an engine's strength and pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specs' suggests specifications, but it is glasses, drawn as OO.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for energy, vigour or force.

clue.text: Qualifier's against cutting new beard

indicators.note: cutting means the letter for against slices into the rearranged letters
new signals the letters of beard are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: V, short for versus, means against

explanation.surface: Someone is opposed to trimming a fresh beard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Qualifier' is a grammar term here, not a competitor; 'new' reorders the beard and 'cutting' slips the versus letter into it.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar an adverb modifies or qualifies a verb, adjective or other adverb.

clue.text: Set out to cover team departures

indicators.note: to cover means the rearranged letters wrap around the team
out signals the letters of set are thrown into disorder

parts.note: XI, eleven, is a football or cricket team

explanation.surface: Plan to insure the side's leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, the size of a cricket or football side; 'out' reorders the first word and 'to cover' wraps it round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Exits are acts of leaving, so they are departures.

clue.text: A bit of nasty ear infection

indicators.note: a bit of means the answer is a part found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Part of an unpleasant ear disease.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed infection of a gland on the eyelid.

clue.text: Indian state's area service rolled back

indicators.note: rolled back means the word for service is read in reverse

parts.note: Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A region of India has its local church service turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a state in north-east India, famous for its tea.

clue.text: Skinny artist

parts.note: skinny seems to mean thin, but read as 'working on skin' it describes someone who draws on bodies

explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinny' looks like a thin painter; really it is an artist whose canvas is skin.
explanation.definitionFit: This person inks designs into clients' skin, so their art is literally skin-based.

clue.text: What might be instrumental in legislative assembly notes?

parts.note: a legislative assembly is a chamber, such as the upper house
music is made of notes

explanation.surface: Speaking notes for use in a parliament might prove decisive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrumental' seems to mean influential, but here it means played on instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Music for a small ensemble of instruments, as in a string quartet, is often purely instrumental.
